qs.q: How many bits make up one nibble?
qs.e: A nibble is made up of 4 bits, which is half of a byte.

qs.q: How many bits make up one byte?
qs.e: A byte is made up of 8 bits, which is two nibbles.

qs.q: What mainly determines how an image is represented digitally?

c.x: What the output device is able to display
The size of the file on the hard disk
The programming language used to build it
The brand of the monitor showing the image

qs.e: Image representation depends on what the output device can display, such as a seven-segment display needing only 7 bits.

qs.q: How many bits are used to represent each pixel in a binary (monochrome) image?
qs.e: A binary image represents each pixel using a single bit.

qs.q: Why is a binary image also called a monochrome image?

c.x: Because it contains no color information at all
Because it is always displayed in a blue tint
Because it requires no storage space to save
Because it is always compressed before saving

qs.e: A binary image is called a 1-bit monochrome image since it contains no color, only black or white per pixel.

qs.q: How many bits are used to represent each pixel in a grayscale image?
qs.e: A grayscale image represents each pixel using 8 bits, stored as one byte.

qs.q: What is the value range of a single pixel in an 8-bit grayscale image?
qs.e: Each pixel in a grayscale image has a gray value between 0 and 255.

qs.q: Approximately how much storage does a 640x480 grayscale image require, given each pixel is stored as one byte?
qs.e: A 640x480 grayscale image, with one byte per pixel, requires about 300 KB of storage.

qs.q: How many bits are used to represent each pixel in a 24-bit color image?
qs.e: A color image represents each pixel using 24 bits.

qs.q: Which three color components together make up each pixel in a 24-bit color image?
qs.e: Each pixel in a 24-bit color image is composed of three values: Red, Green, and Blue.

qs.q: How many distinct colors can a 24-bit color image represent in total?
qs.e: With 256 x 256 x 256 combinations of Red, Green, and Blue, a 24-bit color image supports 16,777,216 possible colors.

qs.q: Approximately how much storage does an uncompressed 640x480 24-bit color image require?
qs.e: A 640x480 24-bit color image without compression requires about 921.6 KB of storage.

qs.q: Which two properties are used to characterize a simple sound wave?
qs.e: A simple sound wave can be characterized by its amplitude and frequency.

qs.q: What happens to a sound as its amplitude increases?
qs.e: The larger the amplitude, the louder the sound.

qs.q: What happens to a sound's tone as its frequency increases?
qs.e: The higher the frequency, the higher the tone.

qs.q: What is the process called in which the voltage of a sound wave is measured at frequent intervals?
qs.e: Sampling is the process of measuring the voltage of a sound wave at frequent intervals.

qs.q: What is the process called in which sampled sound values are stored as a binary code?
qs.e: Decoding is the process of storing the sampled values as a binary code.

qs.q: What is a typical sampling rate mentioned for digitizing a sound wave?
qs.e: The voltage is typically sampled at 48 kHz per second when digitizing sound.

qs.q: How many bits per sample are typically used when decoding a digitized sound wave?
qs.e: Decoding typically stores each sample as a binary code of 16 or 32 bits.

qs.q: What is each individual image in a video sequence called?
qs.e: A video is composed of a sequence of continuous images, and each image is called a frame.

qs.q: Roughly how fast must frames be displayed for a video to appear as continuous movement?
qs.e: Each frame is flashed on the screen for a short time, faster than 50 per second, creating the impression of continuous movement.

qs.q: Why is a standard code needed for representing characters digitally?

c.x: To ensure the same code is used on every computer
To automatically make every file smaller
To allow only a single language to be typed
To increase the processing speed of the CPU

qs.e: A standard is needed to ensure that the code used on your computer is the same as the code used on any other computer.

qs.q: What does the abbreviation ASCII stand for?

c.x: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Advanced System Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for Internal Indexing
Automated Symbol Coding for Information Input

qs.e: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

qs.q: What does the abbreviation EBCDIC stand for?

c.x: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
Enhanced Binary Character Data Input Code
External Byte Coded Decimal Indexing Code

qs.e: EBCDIC stands for Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code.

qs.q: Which company historically used the EBCDIC code on its mainframe computers?
qs.e: EBCDIC was used in the past by IBM mainframes.

qs.q: Why can't ASCII or EBCDIC represent character sets such as Chinese, Arabic, or Japanese?

c.x: They are limited to only 256 possible combinations
These languages have no written characters at all
These codes only support numbers, not letters
These languages require sound instead of text

qs.e: ASCII and EBCDIC are limited to 256 possible combinations, so certain character sets like Chinese, Arabic, and Japanese cannot be represented using them.

qs.q: In ASCII, what is the decimal value of the character 'A'?
qs.e: The character 'A' has a value of 65 in decimal in ASCII.

qs.q: In ASCII, how is the character 'A' (decimal value 65) stored in binary?
qs.e: The character 'A', with decimal value 65, is stored in memory as the binary code 01000001.

qs.q: How many bytes does Unicode use to represent each character?
qs.e: Unicode uses 2 bytes for each character.

qs.q: What is the main disadvantage of Unicode compared to single-byte codes like ASCII?

c.x: It takes twice as much space to store characters
It cannot represent any special symbols at all
It only supports English letters and digits
It requires an internet connection to render

qs.e: Unicode's disadvantage is that it takes twice as much space to store the same number of characters as a single-byte code.
